decisions.question: e-12485

source.question: e-12485
source.value:
The moment of inertia of a plane lamina in the shape of a region $D$ about an axis of rotation $l$ is given by

$$
I_l = \iint\limits_D \lambda (x,y) [r(x,y)]^2 \:\textrm{d}A,
$$

where $\lambda(x,y)$ is the mass density function of the lamina, and $r(x,y)$ is the distance from the line $l$ to the point $(x,y)$ on $D.$

First, notice that $D$ is a type I region with representation

$$
D = \left\{ (x,y) \: : \: 0 \leq x \leq 2, \:\: 2x \leq y \leq x+2 \right\},
$$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14070210/assets/69dcf02cc1883f2b04f81bd6dd486bbe24fedbb813db5778ae3b33ed1fb42e90.png)

     

The distance between a point on $D$ and the line $x=2$ is given by

$$
r(x,y) = |x - 2|.
$$

Therefore, the moment of inertia about the line $x=2$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}I & ={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)[r(x,y)]^{2}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{2x}^{x+2}(\frac{y}{8})|x-2{|}^{2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{2x}^{x+2}(\frac{y}{8})(x-2)^{2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}(x-2)^{2}{\int }_{2x}^{x+2}\frac{y}{8}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}(x-2)^{2}{[\frac{{y}^{2}}{16}]}_{2x}^{x+2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{16}{\int }_{0}^{2}(x-2)^{2}((x+2)^{2}-(2x)^{2})\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{16}{\int }_{0}^{2}({x}^{2}-4x+4)(4+4x-3{x}^{2})\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{16}{\int }_{0}^{2}(16-24{x}^{2}+16{x}^{3}-3{x}^{4})\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{16}{[16x-8{x}^{3}+4{x}^{4}-\frac{3{x}^{5}}{5}]}_{0}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{16}(32-64+64-\frac{96}{5})-0 \\  & =\frac{1}{16}(\frac{64}{5}) \\  & =\frac{4}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

source.value:
The moment of inertia of a plane lamina in the shape of a region $D$ about an axis of rotation $l$ is given by

$$
I_l = \iint\limits_D \lambda (x,y) [r(x,y)]^2 \:\textrm{d}A,
$$

where $\lambda(x,y)$ is the mass density function of the lamina, and $r(x,y)$ is the distance from the line $l$ to the point $(x,y)$ on $D.$

First, notice that $D$ is a type I region with representation

$$
D = \left\{ (x,y) \: : \: 0 \leq x \leq 3, \:\: x \leq y \leq 4x-x^2 \right\},
$$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14070210/assets/6291950b5483f3c102df7249674412c7c11646409cb1b43df604de6bd5ace86f.png)

  

The distance between a point on $D$ and the line $x=3$ is given by

$$
r(x,y) = |x - 3|.
$$

Since the plate has uniform density, the mass density function is given by

$$
\lambda(x,y) = \dfrac{M}{\mathcal{A}} = \dfrac{2M}{9}.
$$

Therefore, the moment of inertia about the line $x=3$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}I & ={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)[r(x,y)]^{2}\,\text{d}A \\  & =\frac{2M}{9}{\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{x}^{4x-{x}^{2}}|x-3{|}^{2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{2M}{9}{\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{x}^{4x-{x}^{2}}(x-3)^{2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{2M}{9}{\int }_{0}^{3}(x-3)^{2}[y]_{y=x}^{y=4x-{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{2M}{9}{\int }_{0}^{3}({x}^{2}-6x+9)(3x-{x}^{2})\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{2M}{9}{\int }_{0}^{3}-{x}^{4}+9{x}^{3}-27{x}^{2}+27x\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{2M}{9}{[-\frac{{x}^{5}}{5}+\frac{9{x}^{4}}{4}-9{x}^{3}+\frac{27{x}^{2}}{2}]}_{0}^{3} \\  & =\frac{2M}{{3}^{2}}(-\frac{{3}^{5}}{5}+\frac{{3}^{6}}{4}-{3}^{5}+\frac{{3}^{5}}{2}) \\  & =2\cdot {3}^{3}M(-\frac{1}{5}+\frac{3}{4}-1+\frac{1}{2}) \\  & =\frac{27M}{10}.\end{aligned}
$$

source.question: e-12488
source.value:
The moment of inertia of a plane lamina in the shape of a region $D$ about an axis of rotation $l$ is given by

$$
I_l = \iint\limits_D \lambda (x,y) [r(x,y)]^2 \:\textrm{d}A,
$$

where $\lambda(x,y)$ is the mass density function of the lamina, and $r(x,y)$ is the distance from the line $l$ to the point $(x,y)$ on $D.$

First, notice that $D$ is a type I region with representation

$$
D = \left\{ (x,y) \: : \: 0 \leq x \leq 1, \:\: 0 \leq y \leq \sqrt x \right\},
$$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14070210/assets/7faaecf39250dbdd1b92d789f6c217afe883c27533b563dae82ed82d228d9b4d.png)

Also, the distance between a point and the line $x=-1$ is given by

$$
r(x,y) = |x-(-1)| = |x+1|.
$$

Next, the mass density can be written as $\lambda(x,y) = k |y| = ky,$ where $k$ is a constant of proportionality. We can find the value of $k$ by integrating the mass density function over the plate.

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{x}}ky\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & =k{\int }_{0}^{1}{[\frac{1}{2}{y}^{2}]}_{0}^{\sqrt{x}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{k}{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}(x-0)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{k}{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}x\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{k}{2}\cdot {[\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{k}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, 

$$
\lambda(x,y) = k y = 4M y.
$$

Therefore, the moment of inertia about the line $x=-1$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{I}_{l} & ={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)[r(x,y)]^{2}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{x}}4My\,|x+1{|}^{2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{x}}4My(x+1)^{2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & =4M{\int }_{0}^{1}(x+1)^{2}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{x}}y\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & =4M{\int }_{0}^{1}(x+1)^{2}{[\frac{1}{2}{y}^{2}]}_{0}^{\sqrt{x}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =2M{\int }_{0}^{1}(x+1)^{2}(x-0)\,\text{d}x \\  & =2M{\int }_{0}^{1}({x}^{3}+2{x}^{2}+x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =2M{[\frac{1}{4}{x}^{4}+\frac{2}{3}{x}^{3}+\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =2M(\frac{1}{4}+\frac{2}{3}+\frac{1}{2}) \\  & =2M\cdot \frac{17}{12} \\  & =\frac{17M}{6}.\end{aligned}
$$
